articles.body: Trinity Rodman will miss the United States women's national team's upcoming CONCACAF W Championship after suffering a minor shoulder injury. US Soccer confirmed her withdrawal on November 24 and named Gotham FC forward Jaedyn Shaw as her replacement. The news came just hours after reports claimed that Rodman and tennis star Ben Shelton had ended their relationship after nearly two years together. Neither athlete has publicly confirmed the reported split. Rodman's injury dates back to the Washington Spirit's 2-1 defeat to Kansas City Current in the NWSL Championship on November 21.Trinity Rodman's Shoulder Injury Rules Her Out as Jaedyn Shaw Takes Her USWNT SpotUS Soccer confirmed that Rodman picked up the injury during the NWSL Championship game. The forward was hurt in the opening minutes after a collision with Kansas City Current defender Laney Rouse. Despite the problem, she returned to the field and stayed in the game.The 24-year-old even scored Washington's only goal in stoppage time, but it was not enough to prevent a 2-1 defeat. The loss also ended the Spirit's hopes of winning the NWSL title.Following the injury, USWNT head coach Emma Hayes brought in Jaedyn Shaw to replace Rodman for the 2026 CONCACAF W Championship. The Gotham FC forward has already made 37 appearances for the national team and scored 10 goals.The tournament is important for the United States as it also serves as qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil. The four quarterfinal winners will earn direct places in the tournament. The competition will also decide the CONCACAF teams for the 2028 Olympic Games.According to the Associated Press, the United States will face El Salvador in its quarterfinal on Friday in Mansfield, Texas.Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman Reportedly End Relationship After Busy Sporting SchedulesRodman's withdrawal came hours after the Daily Mail reported that she and Ben Shelton had separated. The report claimed that their demanding careers and frequent travel made it difficult to spend enough time together. However, the two are reportedly still on good terms.The couple made their relationship public in March 2025 after months of speculation. Since then, they have often travelled to support each other at major sporting events.Rodman was regularly seen cheering for Shelton during his tennis matches. She also attended Wimbledon in 2025 and supported him during his run at the 2026 US Open. At the same time, Shelton also made efforts to attend Rodman's soccer matches.However, their schedules became harder to manage as both athletes continued to travel for their respective sports.Shelton had spoken about this problem in a September interview with Us Weekly. He explained that finding time for each other was not always easy, even when they had a few days away from competition."It is really difficult," Shelton said.He also explained that both athletes were often too tired to make plans after finishing their tournaments."Sometimes I leave these tournaments and I'm a bit of a zombie. I'm not the most fun person to be around," he said.Shelton added that both were still working towards their biggest career goals. He described this period as one of the hardest times for their relationship but said having someone who understood the demands of professional sport helped.Their recent results also came on the same Saturday. Shelton lost his ATP Finals semifinal against Carlos Alcaraz in Turin, while Rodman and the Spirit fell short in the NWSL Championship.The Daily Mail said it had contacted representatives for both athletes for comment. articles.title: OSSAA schools approve recruiting and summer participation rule changes
articles.summary: OSSAA member schools approved two rule changes that address summer participation and recruiting violation, it was announced Wednesday.
articles.body:
Oklahoma Secondary School Activities Association member schools approved two rule changes that address summer participation and recruiting violations, the OSSAA announced Wednesday.

The votes included revisions to Rule 7 and Rule 9.

The change to Rule 7 will take effect at the end of the school year and has to do with summer participation.

It is essentially in place to prevent athletes from scouting a program. Now, participating in summer activities will play a role in determining whether an athlete is tied to that school. If they are, their ability to transfer will be limited.

Certain things — such as weightlifting, strength and conditioning, individual skill camps and spring football — will not count as participation.

The Rule 9 change will take effect on July 1 and is related to the recruitment of athletes.

A committee will now review complaints and hold hearings to determine if violations have occurred.

Coaches who are guilty of recruiting violations will be suspended for 365 days, and athletic programs will be given a one-year warning. Repeated violations for a program will result in more consequences.

"Our dedicated Rule Review Committee has expedited a lot of positive changes," OSSAA executive director David Jackson said in a release. "It's yet another avenue in which we're having in-depth conversations with school leaders to ensure OSSAA is serving students to the best of its ability and setting us up to be more adaptable for years to come."

articles.title: Week 12 Fantasy Football Injury Report: The Latest Update On Bhayshul Tuten, Derrick Henry, And All The Stars
articles.summary: The latest injury updates on all the top fantasy football stars in Week 12.
articles.body:
It's Wednesday, and as always, that means it's time for our first fantasy football injury report of the week. It will be key to check these out and read them closely, because the holiday schedule gives us five games to worry about before we even reach the weekend. This is our mid-week fantasy football injury report for Week 12.

Purdy missed practice on Wednesday due to a sprained ankle. We don't expect him to be in danger of missing Week 12, but this is worth monitoring just in case.

Coming off the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, Darnold is expected to return to action and reclaim his starting job from Drew Lock. He is a slight upgrade over Lock.

Herbert is in the concussion protocol and was not able to practice on Wednesday. You shouldn't be starting Herbert even if he is cleared, but somehow it seems like it would be even worse for the Chargers' weapons if Herbert can't play.

RB Kenneth Walker III, Kansas City Chiefs

Walker has once again been ruled out for the Chiefs on a short week. It will be wheels up for rookie Emmett Johnson again this week.

Henry has been placed in the league's concussion protocol. While the team is expecting him to play this week, he will have to clear the protocol before he's allowed out there. Justice Hill would be the next man up.

Tuten did not practice on Wednesday due to his ankle injury, and he could be shaping up to be a game-time decision this week. Monitor this situation closely. Chris Rodriguez is the next man up.

Marks is back at practice after missing last week due to a concussion. With David Montgomery now back, it will be interesting to see how this backfield plays out. We expect Marks to lead the backfield.

McMillan is dealing with a foot injury, but is expected to play this week. However, his practice status should be monitored throughout the week.

After missing the past few games with a hamstring injury, Harrison was back at practice on Wednesday. He still has not been fully integrated into the Texans' offense after getting injured so quickly after the trade.

WR Michael Pittman Jr, Pittsburgh Steelers

Pittman is once again practicing on Wednesday and is expected to return from IR this week.

Ferguson has been ruled out for Thanksgiving and will miss Week 12.

Kincaid should once again be considered questionable for Week 12 and could go either way after missing Week 11. Dawson Knox will see more work if Kincaid can't go.

articles.body: Los Angeles Sparks star Cameron Brink has shared the first pictures from her wedding to longtime partner Ben Felter, and her fellow WNBA players were quick to congratulate her. The couple got married on November 14 at Stanford Memorial Church in California, returning to the university where their relationship began. Brink posted 20 pictures from the celebrations on Instagram, including several moments with her new husband. Angel Reese, Paige Bueckers and other basketball stars joined the celebrations online, while Caitlin Clark also showed her support by liking the post.Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers Join WNBA Stars in Congratulating Cameron BrinkBrink shared the wedding pictures with a heartfelt message for Felter."Overwhelmed with joy and pride to be your wife.🤍"She also added, "The best day of my life."The post quickly received attention from her fellow players. Angel Reese was among the first to leave a comment, writing, "gorgggg." Dallas Wings star Paige Bueckers also shared her reaction."Just perfect 😍," she wrote.Brink's former Stanford teammate Kiki Iriafen, who now plays for the Washington Mystics, also praised her friend's wedding look."Effortlessly Stunning!! 😍😍," Iriafen commented.Her Mystics teammate Sonia Citron joined in with a short but sweet message, writing, "pretty girl 😍."Meanwhile, Caitlin Clark showed her support by liking Brink's Instagram post. The reactions gave the newly married Sparks star plenty of love from across the basketball world.Cameron Brink and Ben Felter Return to Stanford Where Their Love Story BeganThe wedding was especially meaningful for Brink and Felter because Stanford was where they first met. The couple connected in 2020 through an athlete-matching survey arranged by Brink's then-teammates Lexie and Lacie Hull. Their friendship later turned into a relationship, and they eventually decided to take the next step.Felter proposed in Paris in September 2024. He planned a surprise proposal at the Shangri-La Hotel with the Eiffel Tower in the background. Brink had no idea he was coming to Paris to ask her to marry him.Their wedding ceremony took place at Stanford Memorial Church on November 14. The celebrations later moved to the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay, California.In her interview with Vogue, Brink explained why the church meant so much to her."Walking past the ornate mosaics on my way to class was always the best part of my day," she said.The wedding also brought together some familiar faces from the sports world. Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, attended the celebrations. Ayesha was one of Brink's bridesmaids, while their daughter Ryan served as the flower girl.The families have shared a close bond for years. Brink and Stephen Curry are god-siblings because their parents knew each other during their college days. Their fathers played basketball together at Virginia Tech, while their mothers were roommates.Vogue also shared details about Brink's wedding outfits. She wore four different looks during the celebrations, including custom dresses by Danielle Frankel for the ceremony and reception. Her other outfits came from Di Petsa.The newlyweds arrived at the reception in a 1957 Rolls-Royce. One of the most special moments came during their first dance to "Until I Found You." Ryan Curry sang the song as the couple danced together.For Brink, the wedding brought her back to the place where she first met Felter. articles.title: World Chess Championship: Gukesh draws second game against Javokhir Sindarov in 20 moves; score tied 1-1
articles.summary: D Gukesh settled for a draw with white against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in the second game of the FIDE World Championship in Geneva on Wednesday,
articles.body: D Gukesh settled for a draw with white against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in the second game of the FIDE World Championship in Geneva on Wednesday, with the contest ending after just 20 moves.The reigning world champion, who is not usually known for agreeing to early draws, opted for a repetition of moves after spending some time in the middle game. The two players shared the point, taking their tally to one each after two games of the 14-game match.Playing with white for the first time in the match, Gukesh opened with the London System, possibly looking for a more cautious approach after facing pressure in the opening game, where Sindarov had pushed for an advantage but could not convert it.However, Sindarov was able to equalise through a series of straightforward moves, leaving little room for either player to gain an edge in the middle game. The two exchanged a pair of minor pieces, but all 30 remaining pieces were still on the board when they agreed to a draw.Gukesh's 14th move drew attention, allowing Sindarov to advance a kingside pawn on his next turn by pushing his bishop's pawn forward. Some commentators felt the move had unsettled the Indian. Gukesh responded with a move to stop the pawn's progress, but Sindarov was not under any real pressure thereafter.The players repeated their moves soon after, bringing the game to a close. Sindarov arguably had the better of the opening exchanges, with Gukesh's London System failing to give him any meaningful advantage.With 12 games still to be played in the 14-game match, Sindarov will have the white pieces in the third game and will look to press for an advantage.Asked after the game about his choice of the London System and the quick draw, Gukesh said: "Well it’s a good opening and nowadays everything from both colours are so much playable...so much to explore because of the engines. So, I don’t think one opening is better than the other...it would be a nice way to start the match (with London System)."Asked whether he was frustrated by Sindarov's solid play and the lack of opportunities to push for a win, Gukesh said both players were so well prepared for the championship that a "formal outcome" was to be expected."Yeah, I felt I could have remembered more from my notes, but okay it's like both players are super well prepared and getting nothing out of the opening is a very formal outcome in a wold championship," said Gukesh.He added that he had hoped to catch Sindarov off guard with the London System, but the Uzbek was well prepared and proved a tough opponent."London, I thought, would be a little surprise early in the match, but well done to my opponent, he was prepared and he was tough. London as an opening, I mean somewhere I was playing it quite a bit maybe in the lockdown pandemic so...some nostalgic opening," he said, explaining his choice of the London System.The first player to reach 7.5 points will be crowned champion. In case of a tie after 14 games, shorter-format tiebreak games will be played to determine the winner.The time control is 120 minutes for the first 40 moves, with an additional 30 minutes and a 30-second increment per move from move 41. Draws by mutual agreement are not permitted before the completion of 40 moves. However, a game can end earlier through threefold repetition or stalemate.The total prize fund for the match is USD 2.5 million. Each win is worth USD 200,000, with the remaining prize money to be shared equally. If the match goes into tiebreaks, the winner will take home USD 1.3 million, while the runner-up will receive USD 1.2 million.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Nostalgic opening from lockdown days': Gukesh explains London System choice
articles.summary: D Gukesh, with white, was not really happy about a soft draw one that allowed Javokhir Sindarov equality and almost forced another draw with repetition of
articles.body: D Gukesh, with white, was not really happy about a soft draw one that allowed Javokhir Sindarov equality and almost forced another draw with repetition of moves.The second game of the 14-game World Chess Championship match between the Indian champion and Uzbek challenger ended in a peace treaty inside two hours and just 20 moves of the London System opening (3.Bf4) in Geneva on Wednesday. Except a knight each, the other 30 pieces were on the board (15 each) when the game ended tamely.Before coming out of the players’ lounge to the fan zone and to the press conference, Gukesh was in a mood of self reflection and did not appear happy with how things had panned out despite having the advantage of white pieces. But he regrouped quickly and managed more than a smile while giving a quick reaction to the official broadcast and detailed answers at the media conference.“Away from the board, I have been much happier compared to Singapore (the match against Ding Liren in 2024),” said Gukesh.On how different it is to be at the match without his father accompanying him and instead, with his Bengaluru-based designer friends Shikhar and Charmie, Gukesh said, “Being with friends takes away a lot of the stress. Happy they are here. Also Gayo (second Gajewski) is here and is doing a lot of work. Happy with the setup for this match.”Gukesh opting for the London system is not suspect, but has been played only twice in World Championship matches (Ding beat Nepo in 2022 and Gukesh and Ding split a point in 2024). Though the opening was a mild surprise, Sindarov was up to the task and on the Uzbek’s prepared line (7..Qb6), Gukesh laughed, “I could not recollect what I was doing here. I felt I could have remembered more from my notes ... It was my nostalgic opening from the lockdown days.”“There is a lot of theory in London (system) too. But it was not some deep strategy (to play this).”Gukesh explained that the position was such that he could always hope that Sindarov could go wrong had they continued to play (and avoid three-fold repetition) but it's likely that even he himself could go wrong and there was not much in the position.Black’s 15th move (f5) invited a long thought from Gukesh and after about 30 minutes he responded with f3 and fell about 35 minutes behind needing to make 24 more moves in about 50 mins. Earlier, a new position on the board was reached after Sindarov's queen retreat (Qd8) on the 11th move.The third game will be played on Thursday before Friday’s rest day with Gukesh having black pieces.Moves (Game 2):D Gukesh vs Javokhir Sindarov -- 1. d4 d5 2. articles.title: Mavrik Bourque returns to Dallas and scores his first goal for Nashville in 3-1 win
articles.summary: DALLAS (AP) — Mavrick Bourque scored his first goal for Nashville, getting it against the team that traded him nearly five months ago as the Predators beat D...
articles.body:
DALLAS (AP) — Mavrick Bourque scored his first goal for Nashville , getting it against the team that traded him nearly five months ago as the Predators beat Dallas 3-1 on Wednesday night to end the Stars' five-game winning streak.

Predators goalie Juuse Saros stopped 20 shots, and withstood a flurry of activity in front of his net toward the end of the Stars' only power play with about 5 1/2 minutes left.

Bourque put Nashville ahead to stay when he scored with just under a minute left in the first period, taking a pass from Brady Skjei and then sliding across the center of the circle before sending a wrister past former teammate Jake Oettinger. The 24-year-old Bourque raised both arms in the air and glanced upward with an expression of relief after finally scoring a goal in his 20th game, though he already had five assists.

Oettinger was coming off his NHL-leading fifth shutout three nights earlier in a 1-0 win over Pittsburgh when he had 33 saves. He stopped 24 shots against the Predators, who won for the ninth time in 11 games.

Wyatt Johnston scored with 35 seconds left for the Stars to avoid being shut out for the first time since a 4-0 loss to St. Louis in their season opener Oct. 1. That came between a pair of empty-net goals for Nashville, Ross Colton with 1:11 left and Jack Drury with 15 seconds left.

Dallas traded Bourque because of salary cap issues to the Predators at the start of free agency July 1. Bourque a restricted free agent due for a big bump from his $950,000 salary last season, and got a $33 million, six-year contract ($5.5 million a season) from the Predators.

A first-round draft pick by the Stars in 2020, Bourque made his NHL debut at the end of 2023-24 season. He had 20 goals and 21 assists playing all 82 regular-season games last season.

articles.title: No. 2 Ludlowe completes its first unbeaten regular season with victory over rival Warde
articles.summary: More than 3,800 fans watched Ludlowe beat Warde as the Falcons completed their first unbeaten regular season.
articles.body:
FAIRFIELD - The Ludlowe football team finished what no Falcons squad had before it - an unbeaten regular season - with a 28-15 win over rival Warde on Wednesday night, earning one of the top two seeds in the upcoming Class L playoffs.

The Falcons (10-0) have now qualified for the state tournament three straight years, but will host a CIAC playoff game as the higher seed for the first time in program history and attempt to earn the school's first postseason win.

"10-0 means the world to me. I have been working with these kids since first grade and started playing tackle in fifth grade," Ludlowe quarterback Ryan Love said. "To see the whole town come together for a game is just bigger than football. Even if they are wearing red, it's a great atmosphere and I am so grateful I got to play in this game."

More than 3,800 fans packed Taft Field to watch Ludlowe earn its seventh straight win in the series and keep the Gallagher/Banyas Trophy with the Falcons. Warde leads the all-time series 17-15.

"Who would have thought 10 years ago, when I took the job and was told outright that we would never be .500?" Ludlowe coach Mitch Ross said. "It has been a lot of work, but it has been a labor of love. I love the players, love the coaches and they put everything into it."

Ludlowe, ranked No. 2 in the GametimeCT Top 10 Football Poll, will be one of the top two seeds in the Class L tournament, where it lost in the quarterfinals in each of the past two seasons. It will have to wait for the result of Naugatuck's game Thursday before knowing its seed and opponent.

"We will never forget that we have never won a playoff game here," Love said. "We haven't proved anything in the postseason and I know this team can prove a lot this postseason. I think we can make a run. The sky is the limit for this team."

Warde was eliminated from playoff contention with the loss, but finished 6-4 in the first season under coach Steve Christy.

"I am just so proud of this team," Christy said. "The senior class has set the stage for us. The way we fought today. We easily could have fallen over, but I thought we showed a lot of guts."

Ludlowe led 14-0 at halftime on touchdown passes from Love to Timmy O'Neil and Jackson Danylko, then took a 21-0 lead in the third quarter on a 16-yard run from Love.

Warde got on the board in the third on a pass from Luke Mancuso to AJ Cortina.

Love ran for another touchdown from 34 yards out in the fourth quarter, and the scoring was capped by Warde's Dylan Osserman's 3-yard run.

Ryan Love, Ludlowe: The senior had a hand in all four Ludlowe scores on the day.

"Before I started, there were 10 to 20 people in the stands each game. And now to have three or four thousand, it made me flash back to those New Canaan-Darien games. That's truly how I felt. We have really arrived with 4,000 people here to watch a football game between Ludlowe and Warde. Who would have ever thought we would get to that point?" - Ludlowe coach Mitch Ross.

articles.title: Capitals Glide Past Flyers, 7-3, End Losing Skid
articles.summary: Logan Thompson rebounded from an early goal to shut down Philadelphia, while crucial penalty kills and a clinical offensive explosion snapped Washington’s fr...
articles.body:
The Washington Capitals ended their five game skid Wednesday evening, taking down the Philadelphia Flyers , 7-3, in a critical game to start the second quarter of the season.

Despite an early lapse, the Capitals took control and Logan Thompson stood tall in net — allowing just one goal from the second through the 59th minute of the contest. Washington out-shot the Flyers, 35-21, and blocked 17 shots in the effort to snap the five-game skid.

Washington started off on the wrong foot once again, surrendering a two-on-one chance to the Flyers that resulted in Travis Konecny slotting one past Thompson just 17 seconds into the contest.

"I think I'm used to it by now," Thompson said. "I think I've had, what, 10 games with first shot, first goal? So I know everyone's been all over me for that. But again, sometimes it's a good play. You know, I came out, I tried to force to make the pass, and they made a good play. So I'm just as frustrated as everyone else. I get it. I'm trying. No one beats himself up more than me. But that's just that's just hockey right now."

A shot rebounding off the board behind the net fell for Alex Tuch to serve a puck across the front that Ryan Leonard backhanded home to tie things up at the 3:33 mark of the opening period.

"It certainly affected us, but I didn't think it crushed us," Carbery said of the early hole. "I thought we were able to get back to our game, even though we're down one nothing, and the shifts following, you started to see some good things and our identity play out in those shifts."

The Capitals saw two early power play chances and failed to convert on both, but put together a number of high-danger chances to gain momentum after the early blunder.

Another two-on-one chance for the Flyers came last in the second, but this resulted in a blocked shot by Matt Roy — part of an effort since the opening goal that allowed just four other Philadelphia shots against Logan Thompson, all of which were stopped.

Both sides entrenched themselves in the opening half of the second period despite scoring chances from the opposition, highlighted by Washington killing off three minutes and 24 seconds of penalty time — including 36 seconds of five-on-three play.

"Us being able to kill that off, and [Boone Jenner]'s right there sacrificing his body to make sure that a puck doesn't get to Logan — a great example of of what it takes to win in this league," head coach Spencer Carbery said. "And Boone's right at the front of that with getting in shot lanes, and you kill off a five on three, and then it gives us an opportunity to get back to five on five... It was a huge moment in the game, and Boone deserves a ton of credit for that."

Cole Hutson took possession of the puck on the left board and slithered his way over the left circle before sniping home a power play goal late in the third to give the Capitals a 2-1 advantage — their first lead at home since the second period against New Jersey 11 days prior.

Ivan Miroshnichenko — in his second consecutive game in the lineup — found himself with the puck down the right board, shifted it centrally into the zone toward Joseph Wall and hustled down through the defense to tangle up the netminder and poke the puck free into an empty crease for Boone Jenner to slam it home and give Washington a two-goal advantage headed into the second intermission.

"It was great. I thought Miro played really well tonight," Tuch said. "There was a lot of power play, a lot of PK, so sometimes it's tough to stay in it. But I thought he did a great job. He was physical, he was good defensively, he was skating, and that's that's something when a guy isn't the lineup all the time, I think that's huge. He gives a little bit of momentum, and he came in and made a great play, and got a nice assist out of it."

Through two periods, Washington out-shot the Flyers, 23-16, and blocked 15 shots to relieve pressure on Thompson.

The Capitals successfully killed a Tom Wilson tripping penalty that bled from the second period into the third, but the Flyers knotted one back just under two minutes into the final frame with Rasmus Ristolainen sniping one past Thompson.

Tuch tipped a Liljegren shot from the blue line past Woll to give Washington a multi-goal advantage once again, which the team carried through despite a wild final three minutes.

Matt Roy and Miroshnichenko added unassisted tallies for the Capitals — extending the lead to four goals — before Cole Knuble scored in the final minutes for the Flyers and Dylan Strome ended the night on a good note with 11 seconds left for the home team.

"I think for us, I would say it's mentally important to get a win, to feel the win back on our shoulders, and you know, just keep keep trying to go into points," Alex Ovechkin said.

With the losing skid over, the Capitals look to keep the momentum going and make up for lost chances in the first quarter of the season.

"When you go through a rut like this, and just the amount of negative thoughts and the negative things that just keep piling on, piling on, piling on, to get one behind us and just go 'Okay, we can take a deep breath here.' I think just to get in the win column, and some good things to happen for us, hopefully, that'll help us," Carbery said.

Washington returns to action Friday afternoon, hosting the Florida Panthers at 3 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Dan Muse Rips Penguins Defending
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Penguins coach Dan Muse did not indict his team’s motivation. As the losses mount, the Penguins looked defensively indifferent […]
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Penguins coach Dan Muse did not indict his team's motivation. As the losses mount, the Penguins looked defensively indifferent and absolutely careless with the puck Wednesday in a 6-3 loss to the Calgary Flames.

With respect to Calgary, most of their goals were not hard-earned tallies that culminated in minutes of hard work but rather eye-popping Penguins mistakes and lax coverage bordering on the extreme.

The Penguins coach did not pull an Aaron Rodgers and go scorched earth on his inexplicably casual team, but he was nonetheless angry and direct. "We're just handing out chances there based on puck play and decisions, and we have to be harder to play against around our net. Bottom line."

Indeed, the Penguins gave up five even-strength goals and an empty-netter. Worse, some of the Penguins' best players, Sidney Crosby , Erik Karlsson , and Rickard Rakell , were each a deserved minus-4. Comparatively, Evgeni Malkin was a healthy minus-3 and scored but had three turnovers, though it could have been double that.

Muse also made it clear that the poor defense doesn't fall solely on the defensemen, "I've said it multiple times, you know, a lot of rush defense starts in the offensive zone, and so if we've got three forwards down low and then the (defense) pinches without coverage, it's going to be ugly and we're seeing that."

Third defense pairing Kris Letang and Trevor van Riemsdyk were reduced to net-front spectators on other goals. Muse noticed, "It's another night where it's a lot of self-inflicted wounds."

articles.title: Chad Smith wears Wu-Tang Nikes to meet group; Lions unveil Wu merch
articles.summary: The Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer, who grew up in Metro Detroit, will perform with Wu-Tang Clan during halftime at the Lions game on Thursday.
articles.body:
Chad Smith showed up for soundcheck at Ford Field for his Thanksgiving performance with the Wu-Tang Clan wearing Wu-Tang branded Nike Dunks, the Lions showed in an Instagram video released Nov. 25.

Smith, the Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer who grew up in Bloomfield Hills, is set to join the Wu during their halftime performance during the Lions-Bears game on Nov. 26.

The performance is curated by Eminem and Paul Rosenberg, who are in their second year of a three-year agreement to steer the Thanksgiving halftime show.

In the video, Smith is seen greeting members of the Wu-Tang Clan, the legendary New York rap collective that was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame earlier this month.

Smith is complimented on his kicks, a pair of black and yellow Nike Dunk high-tops branded with the Wu-Tang logo. The shoes were originally released in extremely limited edition in 1999, and were rereleased in 2024 for their 25th anniversary.

"I'm representin', oh yeah!" Smith says, before Wu-Tang's Method Man says to the camera, "now who else can hang out with a Chili Pepper?"

Wu-Tang was announced as the halftime performer on Nov. 1 . Paul Rosenberg, Eminem's manager, told The Detroit News the selection of Wu-Tang is "a bullseye" in terms of what he and Eminem want for the show.

"When the idea of Wu-Tang came up, we just all thought A) it's going to be really unexpected, which we love, and B) we thought it was a bullseye for the right sort of association with the thing that Marshall and myself are passionate about, which his hip-hop," he said . "The idea of a Wu-Tang Thanksgiving seems so awesome that we went for it."

Smith was announced as a guest performer with the Staten Island group on Nov. 20 .

"Obviously Chad being from Michigan and being a huge Lions fan, it just made sense, and the band loved the idea as well," Rosenberg said.

The Lions also unveiled several specialized Wu-Tang merch items that will be available at Thursday's game. They include a Wu-Tang Lions shirt (which reads "Shaolin to the Motor City" on the back), a Wu-Tang Forever T-shirt with a Lions logo at the center, and a Wu-Tang/ Lions crossover hoodie and crew neck sweatshirt.

(To see the items, scroll to slide 5 in the post below.)

The Wu-Tang/ Lions merchandise will be available at the game at Lions Supply inside Gate A, according to the Instagram post.

Kickoff for Thursday's game is scheduled for 1:02 p.m.

articles.title: A conversation with UNM swimming and diving's Elsa Reel
articles.summary: Reel, who hails from Christoval, Texas and went to high school in nearby San Angelo, established UNM records in the 100-meter breaststroke (1 minute, 1.23 se...
articles.body:
Reel, who hails from Christoval, Texas and went to high school in nearby San Angelo, established UNM records in the 100-meter breaststroke (1 minute, 1.23 seconds) and the 200 individual medley (2:02.0) last weekend at the Phil Hansel Invitational in Houston. She spoke with the Journal on Tuesday at UNM's Student Support and Services Center.

Elsa, how long have you been swimming, and how did you get your start? I started when I was 6. We had this after-school program at San Angelo Central High School, so all the local kids would go and swim if they wanted to swim. I did that for probably seven years and started doing club when I was 10. Then I transferred schools so I could continue swimming, and I've been doing it ever since.

Do you have a favorite event? I'd say my specialty is the 100 breaststroke. But since I've been here I've been focusing a lot on the (200) breast and I've been trying to hold my speed on the 100 and just keep going for the two breast.

How did you wind up at UNM? I started talking to Naya (Higashima, UNM's head swim coach) my junior year, and then I went on an unofficial visit and really liked it. I came back my senior year, at the very beginning, and went on an official visit with four other girls, and two of them on my visit committed with me. I just actually love it here. The team is so amazing. I love the city, I love Albuquerque. I love the mountains here. The coaching and how many resources we have here is just so amazing.

What are the main adjustments you had to make in transitioning from high school to college? In high school, I feel like I was more focused on school. I went to school for six or seven hours a day, and then I had practice for like three. Then you come here and you go to school for like two hours a day and then you practice, you're at (weight training) and you go to the training room for treatment and you're at study hall. It's like swim is your life instead of school being your life.

(Make no mistake, Reel is a serious student. She came to UNM with 82 advanced placement and dual credits. Despite her first-year status as an athlete, she's classified academically as a fourth-year student.)

What's your major, and how do you hope to use your degree? I'm a biology major, and I'm on the pre-med track. Trying to get into med school is the goal.

What's your favorite class? Org chem (organic chemistry). … I enjoy learning, and I enjoy getting to know all the different reactions. I just love learning different things.

Favorite athlete: Olympic gold medalist swimmer Gretchen Walsh

Last book read: "Man's Search for Meaning" by Viktor Frankl

Last movie seen: "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" with teammates. "We had a blast. It was so good. So sad."

What she listens to: "A lot of different types:" recently, Drake, Future, Bryson Tiller, Kings of Leon, the Lumineers

Up Next: U.S. Open-Long Course, Dec. 2-5, Austin, Texas

articles.title: Ex-Cricket Australia boss James Sutherland defends ‘Sandpapergate’ probe
articles.summary: Meanwhile, David Warner denies a broadcaster’s claim that he used superglue and grit to tamper with the ball.
articles.body:
Former Cricket Australia (CA) chief James Sutherland defended his handling of the 2018 “ Sandpapergate ” investigation on Thursday, but refused to weigh in on the crisis tearing the sport apart.

Sutherland was at the helm when the ball-tampering scandal erupted during the third Test at Cape Town against South Africa.

A whirlwind Cricket Australia investigation laid the blame on then-captain Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner, and Cameron Bancroft , the player who used sandpaper to rough up the ball to make it swing.

Retired Australian opener Usman Khawaja reopened old wounds this month by alleging in his autobiography that the whole team was aware of what was going on, claims backed by Warner and Bancroft.

It led to current captain Pat Cummins vigorously denying he or the bowlers at the time – Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon – were in on the plot.

“I don’t look back on if things could, or should, have been dealt with differently,” said Sutherland, who stepped down in the wake of the crisis and is now head of Golf Australia.

“We did the best we could with the situation that was in front of us and the information in front of us,” he added to The Australian newspaper.

“It was a tough time and a very, very difficult situation for me personally. I’m not going to speak for other people. I know lots of people found it difficult.

“I believe I’m out of it now, and [current CA boss] Todd [Greenberg’s] job is hard enough without me speaking about it.”

Cricket Australia, under Greenberg, has ruled out reopening the probe but is setting up a forum for players to share their experiences about 2018.

Interim CA chairman David Boon also made clear there would be no new sanctions coming out of it.

In a separate interview with the Sydney Morning Herald on the sidelines of the Australian PGA Championship in Sydney, Sutherland said it would be inappropriate to comment on Khawaja’s claims .

“I’ve made that personal commitment that I wouldn’t make comments from afar on current cricket issues. I’ve been true to that so far,” he said.

“It’s fair to say it brings back some memories and not too many happy memories. I just recall it being an incredibly intense and stressful period.”

Warner hits back over ‘unverified’ superglue, grit ball-tampering claims

Warner has hit out at Melbourne-based broadcaster Gerard Whateley’s claims that the former Australia Test opener used superglue and grit on finger strapping to tamper with the ball.

A long-form investigation published by News Corp and SEN Radio claimed Warner’s finger strapping was found in South Africa and investigated by an official from the International Cricket Council, the sport’s governing body.

Commenting on an Instagram post discussing Whateley’s report, Warner labelled those claims “unverified” and accused the media of “perpetuating speculation” around his involvement in the ball-tampering scandal.

“I’m not entirely sure where Gerard’s assertions have come from, as they certainly do not align with my recollection of events,” Warner said.

“In relation to the alleged use of superglue and grit, and the more recent claims regarding the finger, could I respectfully ask what credible evidence exists to substantiate these allegations?

“Before further unverified claims are circulated publicly, I would suggest establishing the facts rather than perpetuating speculation.”

Warner, who was banned for a year over his role in the 2018 scandal, commented again in response to another user, questioning “the distinction between journalism and bullying”.

“Education and eloquence are admirable qualities, but they should never be used to undermine those who weren’t afforded the same opportunities,” Warner wrote.

“When someone uses their public platform to control a narrative without affording others the same voice, it raises a legitimate question about the distinction between journalism and bullying.”

Last weekend, Warner and Khawaja were taken off television commentary duties by Fox Sports. The move came after Cummins’s lengthy news conference and days after Warner blasted CA’s handling of Sandpapergate as “a cover-up”.

articles.title: Palestine coach says team represents suffering but also offers hope
articles.summary: Despite navigating personal hardships, Ihab Abu Jazar calls it a ‘badge of honour’ to coach the Palestine football team.
articles.body:
For Ihab Abu Jazar, being the coach of Palestine’s national football team comes with burdens far heavier than sporting responsibilities.

His mind constantly returns to his family in Gaza, now displaced and living in tents amid Israel’s genocidal war on the Palestinian territory.

“Truthfully, it is difficult to carry out your professional responsibilities while your family and your people are living through such circumstances,” he told Al Jazeera earlier this month while in Doha.

“For me to coach the Palestinian national team, a team that represents this suffering, and to try to make it a source of joy, bring a smile to people’s faces or give the Palestinian people hope, means a great deal to me personally.”

The 46-year-old former footballer said it was a “badge of honour” to coach the national team, which he led to 2027 AFC Asian Cup qualification after taking the reins in 2024.

The team were drawn in Group A against Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Oman, with the tournament rescheduled from January to December 2027 due to the ongoing conflict in the region.

Palestine have enjoyed considerable success in recent international friendlies, including a 2-2 draw with New Zealand, defeating Tajikistan 4-2, and thrashing China 5-0.

But the victories are bittersweet, given what’s happening at home.

He was in Algeria for a training camp with the national team when he received news that his house had been destroyed. His entire family now lives in al-Mawasi, a coastal area where more than 900,000 displaced people are sheltering in southern Gaza.

“The Palestinian people are suffering wherever they are,” Abu Jazar said.

He recounted an ordeal he went through before a qualifying match against Kuwait. Israel had issued a forced evacuation order for the area where his family lived, but his brother, Khalil, refused to leave.

“He had reached a point where he was simply saying, ‘Where am I supposed to go? Where can I possibly go?’” Abu Jazar recalled.

He made a last-ditch attempt to convince his brother to flee before boarding the team bus headed to the stadium for the match.

“I kept trying to call, but I could not get through. At that point, I had to trust that, God willing, my brother had listened to what I told him,” Abu Jazar said.

“We also had a match to play in the name of Palestine. We had to concentrate and do our job.”

Abu Jazar was able to breathe a sigh of relief after the match when he eventually got through to his brother, who assured him that they had all managed to leave safely.

A passion for sport is shared throughout Abu Jazar’s family. His mother, Huda, played volleyball at school and even offers her son tactical advice over the phone.

“Sometimes we talk about football and sports; she evaluates the players and discusses their performances after a match,” he said. “To be honest, she understands football very well in general.”

Abu Jazar’s message to the world is: “We are a people who simply want to live. We are a people with ambitions and hopes, a people with creative minds, thinkers, and scientists.

“And sport is also part of the culture and identity of any society. We, too, are sporting people; we are football-loving people.

“So, we ask the whole world to grant us our rights.”

articles.title: El Málaga asume pérdidas de 2,3 millones en 2025-2026 tras el hito del ascenso a Primera
articles.standfirst: El club batió los 25 millones de facturación ordinaria, con un alza del 26% e incrementos en todas las áreas
articles.summary: El club batió los 25 millones de facturación ordinaria, con un alza del 26% e incrementos en todas las áreas
articles.body: El Málaga CF asume pérdidas tras el hito de su vuelta a Primera División. El nuevo club de LaLiga EA Sports cerró 2025-2026 con unos números rojos de 2,3 millones de euros, rompiendo así con dos temporadas consecutivas en las que había generado beneficios, según datos extraídos de Intelligence 2P, la unidad de estrategia e inteligencia de mercado de 2Playbook. La explicación a este déficit se encuentra, en parte, en el fuerte incremento del gasto en personal. Una partida en la que se incluyen tanto los variables por rendimiento deportivo que tienen hoy la mayoría de contratos de futbolistas, como las primas colectivas pactadas con el vestuario. Sólo en este último punto, el Málaga destinó 3,8 millones de euros, de los que 3,3 millones fueron a parar a la plantilla del primer equipo (aquí también se cuenta al entrenador y parte del staff técnico). Con todo ello, el gasto en personal deportivo se disparó un 56% interanual, hasta 15,1 millones de euros. Si se incluye a la totalidad de profesionales que trabajan en el club, este coste ascendió a 19,5 millones, un 50% por encima respecto al cierre de 2024-2025. La plantilla completa la componían 282 personas a 30 de junio de 2026. También crecieron los otros de gastos de explotación, hasta un 25%, para un total de 8,7 millones de euros. Las amortizaciones por fichajes continuaron siendo bajas, situándose por debajo del millón, mientras que el resto de amortizaciones superaron los 3 millones de euros, con un alza del 11% interanual. Estos aumentos en el gasto se compensaron en buena parte con cifras de récord de facturación para el club en Segunda División. Salvo en los ingresos audiovisuales (en 2018-2019 cobró 20 millones de ayuda al descenso), tanto comercial como las patas de abonados y estadio estuvieron en máximos en su periplo por la categoría de plata. El ticketing y otros ingresos por competiciones doblaron la facturación, hasta rozar los 4,3 millones, gracias al mayor número de partidos disputados con la fase de ascenso. Por abonos y carnés de socios, el Málaga recaudó casi 4 millones, un 6% más interanual. El cuarto puesto en la temporada regular se tradujo en 6,6 millones por derechos audiovisuales de LaLiga, un 19% más respecto a 2024-2025. Sin embargo, a diferencia de lo que sucede con muchos equipos de la categoría, la tele no es su principal sustento económico del Málaga CF. Para el club costasoleño, el área comercial es clave. Ya viene siendo su principal línea de negocio en los últimos años, y en la temporada del ascenso no fue menos. Los patrocinios y el merchandising aportaron 10,8 millones de euros, un 21% más interanual. Esta cifra supera a muchos clubes incluso de Primera División. En este punto destaca la aportación pública del Ayuntamiento de Málaga y la Diputación de Málaga, que entre ambos alcanzaban los 1,3 millones de euros como patrocinadores principales. Además, la entidad blanquiazul cuenta con Hummel como socio técnico y otros socios premium como MGS Seguros. Asimismo, el club prefirió esta última temporada no desprenderse de talento –en buena parte, formado en su cantera– para cuadrar los números. En 2024-2025, los casi 5 millones en plusvalías por traspasos fueron claves para mantenerse en la rentabilidad. En cuanto al balance, el club, que sigue bajo gestión del administrador judicial José María Muñoz, se mantiene con fondos propios positivos, aunque con las pérdidas generadas redujera esta cifra hasta los 1,2 millones de euros. Asimismo, la deuda financiera neta creció un 8% y se situaba por encima de los 32 millones de euros a 30 de junio de 2026. Nunca había superado la barrera de los 30 millones en la última década. En su informe, el Málaga no ofrece previsiones de la presente temporada, en la que sólo con los derechos audiovisuales de Primera División tiene garantizados más de 40 millones de euros de facturación. Además, el Ayuntamiento ha redoblado su apoyo al club con un contrato de patrocinio de 1,6 millones de euros, Unicaja ha renovado hasta 2030 y se ha situado como partner estratégico, mientras que la marca local Cervezas Victoria luce ahora su logo en el frontal del pantalón.

articles.title: Luis Milla, en Radio MARCA: "Irme al Como es la mejor decisión que podía haber tomado"
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista analiza en 'La Pizarra de Quintana' el gran momento del equipo italiano, el impacto de Cesc Fàbregas y su decisión de cambiar el Getafe por una aventura que le ha llevado hasta la Champions
articles.summary: El centrocampista analiza en 'La Pizarra de Quintana' el gran momento del equipo italiano, el impacto de Cesc Fàbregas y su decisión de cambiar el Getafe por una aventura que le ha llevado hasta la Champions
articles.body: Luis Milla está viviendo uno de los momentos más especiales de su carrera. A sus 31 años, el centrocampista ha encontrado en el Como el escenario perfecto para disfrutar del fútbol, debutar en la Champions League y convertirse en una pieza importante de un proyecto que está sorprendiendo en Europa. Su golazo y su actuación, premiada con el MVP, en la última victoria del conjunto italiano son una muestra más de su felicidad. Una felicidad que compartió en 'La Pizarra de Quintana', de Radio MARCA, donde repasó su presente y habló de algunos de los nombres propios de su equipo. Uno de ellos es Nico Paz. Preguntado por si ve al joven futbolista preparado para regresar al Real Madrid y tener un papel importante en el conjunto blanco, Milla no tuvo ninguna duda: "Sí, yo le veo de esa altura". El centrocampista fue más allá de su enorme calidad técnica y quiso destacar aspectos de su juego que, a su juicio, marcan la diferencia. "Lo tenéis que ver entrenar, repetir esfuerzos y ayudarnos en el campo a la presión. Es el primero que repliega", explicó. Para Milla, el compromiso y la humildad de Nico Paz son tan importantes como su talento: "Tener la humildad que tiene para trabajar y para ayudarnos, siendo ya una estrella de la Serie A como se le considera, dice mucho de él como persona y como compañero". Eso sí, el futbolista del Como dejó claro que no tiene ninguna prisa por perder a su compañero: "Dejádmelo aquí unos años, que yo tengo un contrato y quiero disfrutarlo aquí". Otro de los grandes protagonistas de la entrevista fue Cesc Fábregas. Milla explicó cómo se ha adaptado a una propuesta futbolística muy diferente a la que conoció durante su etapa en el Getafe. El Como apuesta por un fútbol dinámico, con intercambios de posiciones y mucha libertad para que sus jugadores interpreten los espacios y los momentos del partido. "Es una forma diferente, tenemos muchas cosas diferentes a lo que yo vivía en el Getafe el año pasado", reconoció. El centrocampista destacó que el equipo trabaja cada semana para identificar dónde puede hacer daño a sus rivales, aunque también necesita que sus futbolistas tengan personalidad para tomar decisiones sobre el terreno de juego. "El míster insiste mucho en la personalidad de cada uno para entender los momentos y dónde podemos hacer daño al rival", explicó. Una libertad que, sin embargo, no significa ausencia de estructura: "Hay un gran orden en cuanto a una estructura que trabajamos cada semana". Milla también quiso detenerse en la capacidad de Cesc para transmitir sus ideas y convencer a sus futbolistas. "Tiene una capacidad de llegar al jugador y de convencerle muy grande. Para mí es una de las cosas más importantes de un entrenador", señaló. Además, destacó la precocidad de su trayectoria en los banquillos: "No deja de ser que ha llegado al fútbol profesional de entrenador hace dos años y medio o tres años. Es una cosa increíble". El fichaje por el Como fue una de las decisiones más importantes de la carrera de Luis Milla. Después de su etapa en el Getafe, el centrocampista apostó por un proyecto que le ofrecía la posibilidad de competir en la élite europea y trabajar a las órdenes de Cesc Fàbregas. Ahora, varios meses después, tiene claro que acertó. "En algún momento podrías haber tenido dudas de todas las situaciones que podrían haber surgido, pero ahora mismo, y desde hace mucho tiempo que llegué aquí, me voy dando cuenta de que la decisión que he tomado es la mejor que podía haber tomado", afirmó. El futbolista se mostró especialmente agradecido con las personas que le ayudaron a dar el paso y con un club que, según explicó, cuida todos los detalles para que sus jugadores puedan ofrecer su mejor versión. "Estoy disfrutando como un enano del día a día de un club que hace todo para que el jugador esté bien, para que rinda a su máximo nivel", añadió. Milla también desveló que mantuvo conversaciones con Fàbregas durante el verano. Unas charlas que le ayudaron a comprender el proyecto y a tomar la decisión definitiva. El Como se ha convertido en una de las grandes sorpresas de la Champions League. Con 12 puntos en su casillero y una plantilla con poca experiencia en la competición, el conjunto italiano está firmando un estreno sobresaliente. "Que tengamos 12 puntos a estas alturas tiene un mérito terrible", reconoció Milla, que recordó que se trata de la primera participación del club en el torneo y que cuentan con un equipo muy joven. El centrocampista también puso en valor la dificultad de competir en una competición de este nivel: "Estamos disfrutando mucho de esta competición". Uno de los próximos retos será el enfrentamiento ante el Betis, otro de los equipos revelación, con el que compartirán protagonismo en las próximas jornadas europeas. La experiencia tiene, además, un componente emocional muy especial para el futbolista. Su hermana y nuestra compañera Paula participó en la entrevista y recordó la emoción que vivió la familia al presenciar el gol de Luis en Champions y recoger el premio al MVP. "Cuando metió el gol nos mirábamos, llorera por todos lados. Mi madre emocionada, mi padre igual. No sabíamos qué hacer, saltando, gritando", relató.

articles.title: Jacob Fatu, Becky Lynch and Most Likely Heel and Face Turns at WWE Survivor Series: WarGames 2026
articles.summary: WWE is preparing for a massive Survivor Series: WarGames inside Dalkin Park in Houston, Texas.
articles.body:
WWE is preparing for a massive Survivor Series: WarGames at Daikin Park in Houston on Saturday night.

The Bloodline and The 946 will look to settle their dispute inside the double cage, while Charlotte Flair and Jade Cargill will lead their teams into the dangerous structure.

Becky Lynch is hoping to take the Women's World Championship from Liv Morgan, and Cody Rhodes and CM Punk will head Team USA against Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico in the return of the traditional Survivor Series elimination match.

How will WWE spice up these team battles? Who could turn heel or face to deliver a lasting moment at Survivor Series?

The battle between The Bloodline and The 946 has reached an even playing field, which does not favor Royce Keys and his team.

Roman Reigns has stepped into WarGames before with The Usos, winning multiple times. He has also fought with and against Solo Sikoa.

Keys, Carmelo Hayes, Cruz Montana, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price have no experience in this environment but desperately need to pull off this upset.

The best answer would be for The 946 to have a man on the inside, someone who can help them once the cage door is locked tight.

Fatu's long history with Keys , going back to their indie days, makes him the most obvious candidate. Sikoa would also make sense, since he opposed The Bloodline until this recent alliance.

Both would be better served out of Reigns' shadow, though The 946 is already a large enough group.

It might be best for one of them to turn in order to spite The Tribal Chief rather than truly help The 946. But either move would make sense as a bold setup for a future main event player.

Becky Lynch is almost a babyface by usual metrics already. She is the fan favorite combating The Judgment Day, teaming up with both Stephanie Vaquer and Iyo Sky.

However, The Man is better classified as a tweener. Her team-ups have been contentious, and she has shown no interest in making friends.

She is a lone wolf running into a fight with all of The Judgment Day, and unless she can convince Sky, Sol Ruca and others in conflict with the faction to help her, she is unlikely to beat Morgan.

It would be a shame if Lynch had no plan to counteract any interference, but she hasn't exactly worked to build friendships in her recent run.

The only option to push The Man to a victory would be a defection within The Judgment Day, which is also possible.

Instead of Becky Lynch fully turning face, perhaps she could find an ally in a woman she has been talking up in recent weeks.

Roxanne Perez is the odd woman out in The Judgment Day. She has found little success in the group while both Liv Morgan and Raquel Rodriguez have held singles gold.

What was once a friendship now looks increasingly contentious, as Perez treats Morgan as the only woman deserving of lasting success.

Perez could choose this moment as her chance to break away, costing Morgan the same title she has helped protect for months.

This would fit especially if The Prodigy takes Lynch up on her offer for a mentorship. Perez would not even need to fully turn face, instead joining The Man as an obnoxious tweener team at the top of the Raw roster.

Cody Rhodes needs a refresh, and nothing seems to be working to get him on track.

His feuds with John Cena and Randy Orton were supposed to establish that Rhodes can work with an edge, but it is not translating to his in-ring work.

The American Nightmare came off punting The Viper to play buddy-buddy with CM Punk, who has had no questions about Rhodes' current motivation.

It would make sense for this to all lead to Rhodes vs. Punk, making up for an underwhelming match at SummerSlam between the two with a full-scale rivalry.

The best path to that feud would be for The American Nightmare to turn against The Best in the World after a loss to Team Mexico.

If WWE takes this path, it makes the Team USA vs. Team Mexico match matter and would give SmackDown a real hook going forward into 2027.

What would a heel Rhodes look like? Hopefully, he would be a bold and different character than he has shown so far in WWE.

The answer to that question might have seemed obvious for a long time, but his direction has been murky at best over the past year.

After Rollins suffered an injury in October 2025, The Vision turned on him, just as he was finding his footing as Raw's top heel.

Since returning, The Visionary has settled back into a familiar babyface role, with dynamics that date back to Cody Rhodes' return at WrestleMania 38.

It is time for Rollins to chart a new course, resetting his role after a brief stumble last year.

That could come from the Team USA vs. Team Mexico match, since Rollins is clearly reveling in causing drama for U.S. co-captains Rhodes and CM Punk.

It would be easy for Rollins not to take this match seriously and focus far more on causing problems for two of WWE's top babyfaces and revealing his true intentions for 2027 and beyond.

articles.title: CFP selection committee continues to churn out inexplicable, indefensible rankings | Ian Miller
articles.summary: The Indiana Hoosiers dropped six spots in the College Football Playoff rankings after an overtime loss to Washington, while Alabama fell just three.
articles.body: The College Football Playoff selection committee released its updated rankings Tuesday evening to, well, less controversy than a typical week. There was movement near the top of the rankings, thanks to the UCLA Bruins suffering their first loss of the season in triple overtime at Michigan and the Indiana Hoosiers falling in overtime to the Washington Huskies in Seattle. Then there's the Tennessee Volunteers-Alabama Crimson Tide debate, which this week resulted in a long-awaited changing of the order between the two teams. After weeks of the Crimson Tide sitting above UT, despite a head-to-head loss, the Volunteers jumped them to sit at No. 5. That might have been reasonable, considering the committee's absurd "logic," but there's plenty from this week's poll that isn't. And it's yet again a sign of how the committee just makes things up as they go. CFP SELECTION COMMITTEE HAS OFFICIALLY DISCREDITED ITSELF WITH LATEST RANKINGS First? How they've handled the Hoosiers this season, and particularly the last few weeks. Just three polls ago, Indiana was ranked No. 4 by the selection committee. After not playing for a bye week, they dropped all the way to No. 9. That was bizarre enough, considering again, they didn't play. The committee's excuse for this was that all of the Hoosiers' Big Ten opponents lost in the same week, devaluing their strength of schedule. We'll come back to that. After the bye week, Indiana beat the then-No. 18 team, the USC Trojans, at home by two scores. It moved up just one spot to No. 8. Ahead of this week's poll, the Hoosiers lost on the road to overtime to a team now ranked in the selection committee's own poll. They dropped six spots. Six. So it didn't play, beat a top-15 team by two scores, lost on the road in overtime to a ranked team, and dropped from No. 4 to No. 14. This would never happen to a team from say, another conference that enjoys enhanced protection from consequences. When the Georgia Bulldogs lost, at home, to an unranked Auburn team, they dropped four spots in the AP Top 25. Yes, the AP poll uses a different set of voters, but it's indicative of the different standards applied to different conferences. BIG TEN FACES ONE-BID NIGHTMARE IN CFP RANKINGS AS SEC EYES FOUR BIDS AND BIG 12 COULD THRIVE What makes the Indiana ranking even more, shall we say, confusing, is how it compares to say, Alabama. The committee had a golden opportunity to keep their standards consistent when all of Alabama's SEC wins lost in the same week between the second and third polls. Had they applied the same logic to the Tide as they did with Indiana, they'd have dropped multiple spots. They didn't move at all. This week presented another opportunity for consistency. All of Alabama's SEC wins lost again, except for Mississippi State who beat FCS Tennessee Tech 34-16, which may or may not have counted as a Quality SEC Win™. Alabama dropped just three spots. They're now No. 6, while the Hoosiers are eight places behind them at No. 14. With the same record. Now, there are multiple ways to evaluate records, strength of schedule and overall resume. But the committee seemingly prioritizes how teams perform against their own rankings. This is a terrible idea that inevitably creates circuitous logic, but it's how they've chosen to operate. Ok, fine. Taking them at their word, here's how Alabama has done against teams currently ranked in the CFB playoff top-25: That's it. This is the strength of schedule that boosts the Tide's resume, in the committee's mind, to worthy of being eight spots ahead of Indiana with the same record. Surely though, Indiana must have played an easy schedule that justifies such a lower spot in the poll...right? Well, for comparison, here's how the Hoosiers have done against currently ranked teams: So they've played two more games against ranked opponents, and what do you know? They actually won two of those games! Their two losses have come by a combined seven points, including one to a top-5 quality Ohio State team with its starting quarterback healthy. That came down to one of the last plays of the game. We can also look at ESPN's SP+ to point out how absurd the disparity is. While the perception is that Indiana's played an easy schedule, because of its non-conference opponents, nobody makes that claim about the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs. Even though Georgia, by an objective analytics-driven measurement, has played an easier schedule than Indiana. And a similarly week non-conference slate. Here's how the two schedules compare in SP+ rankings: Indiana Georgia Interesting. Also per SP+, Indiana's schedule ranks as the 38th hardest in the country. Georgia is 44th. Alabama is 14th, so harder than the Hoosiers, but again, they have the same record. The difference does not justify an eight spot differential. Heck, Miami's played a tougher schedule than Georgia, yet they somehow sit at No. 7 in the poll behind not one, not two, but three two-loss SEC teams. Despite the same number of losses, and its one loss coming down to a controversial incomplete pass call late in the fourth quarter on the road to a top-5 team. Not Auburn. In fact, speaking of SEC teams getting the benefit of the doubt, Tennessee's strength of schedule is just 22nd, and they're 1-1 against teams currently ranked in the top-25. Their non-conference schedule, like Georgia's and Indiana's, is embarrassingly bad. They beat up on Furman 56-9, the same awful Georgia Tech team 45-24, and Kennesaw State 42-9. Its loss to South Carolina looks worse than Indiana's two losses now, and they have fewer wins over ranked teams. Why is it nine spots ahead of Indiana with a relatively comparable schedule? The answer, as always, is perception. And selection committee chair Hunter Yurachek confirmed that in his typically embarrassing post-poll interview. When asked why the switch between Tennessee and Alabama, Yurachek basically said the committee just felt like it. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "When we first ranked Alabama at No. 3 two weeks ago, the resume looked different than it did when we started the ranking process this week. So much so that the committee felt that both Texas and Notre Dame deserved to be ranked ahead of Alabama," he told Rece Davis. "And then you couple that with a UCLA loss, and the Indiana loss, and then a Tennessee win against LSU, Tennessee moves up to a point where they’re now directly comparable to Alabama. You got the head-to-head, Tennessee over Alabama. And that’s the switch where you have Texas at 3 now, Notre Dame at 4, Tennessee at 5, and Alabama at 6." Why does beating an unranked 6-5 LSU team make Tennessee comparable to Alabama? What has Alabama actually accomplished besides losing its two toughest games of the year? When asked about Indiana, he gave an even more rambling and incoherent answer. "For the last six weeks, Indiana's had six one-score games. Three out of the last four have been in overtime. And until Saturday, they had found a way to win those games," he said. This is wrong. Indiana beat USC 27-13 roughly 10 days ago. Does the committee not know the outcomes of the games? Because that is factually incorrect. Unfortunately for America, he wasn't done there. "But Saturday, they did not," he continued. "They fell behind the team like a Texas Tech with one loss and then they were in direct comparison with their counterparts in the Big 10 in Oregon and Iowa. You got both of those teams. Oregon has won four games in a row. Iowa has also won four games in a row. Oregon has a win at Ohio State. Iowa lost at home to Ohio State." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Why was Indiana only in direct comparison to other Big Ten teams? Do the two-loss SEC teams not exist? Or is the committee so hopelessly inept and biased that they think two-loss Alabama and Tennessee simply can't be compared to the Big Ten because they're in the mighty SEC and play in big stadiums or something? Four of Indiana's last six games have been against teams currently ranked in the top-25, so why would it be surprising they were close? Though again, it did beat USC by two scores, which Yurachek got wrong. Does he and the committee also think beating OSU without Julian Sayin is the same as beating it with him? Because Oregon's win was after his injury, and Iowa and Indiana's losses were before the injury. Incompetence all the way down. Or maybe they're just mad because Cignetti continues to call out the committee's obvious bias. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Tennessee lost one of its last four games, and their three ensuing wins have come over teams that are a combined 0-9 in their last nine. In fact, Tennessee's resume SP+ is No. 10, while Indiana is No. 11 and UCLA is No. 9. Tennessee is ranked nine spots ahead of Indiana and four spots ahead of UCLA. Guess that doesn't matter though! Cause SEC! What these inconsistencies and illogical arguments boil down to is that the committee believes losses in the SEC shouldn't matter much. They believe that the SEC deserves preferential treatment it hasn't earned, particularly considering that conference's atrocious record in the playoff the past three seasons. There's a very real chance the Big Ten, which undoubtedly has a stronger middle class than the SEC this year, only gets one team in the tournament. While the SEC will get four. And we already know that the SEC conference championship game can't hurt the loser, a ridiculous fact Joey Galloway thankfully brought up on ESPN's show, to great consternation and disappointment from Rece Davis and Heather Dinich. Ranked wins don't matter, objective resumes don't matter, the only thing that matters is perception. Which is why this poll will continue to be a discrediting embarrassment.

articles.title: La reina Letizia juega a la boccia en la Zarzuela con 'El Langui'
articles.standfirst: El cantante, actor y director de cine es miembro de la selección nacional de esta disciplina paralímpica
articles.summary: El cantante, actor y director de cine es miembro de la selección nacional de esta disciplina paralímpica
articles.body: La reina Letizia practicó este jueves la boccia con la selección nacional de esta disciplina paralímpica en el Palacio de la Zarzuela y con uno de sus integrantes más conocidos, el cantante, actor y director de cine Juan Manuel Montilla, 'El Langui'. Fue en una audiencia con la selección de boccia, una de las disciplinas paralímpicas más representativas del deporte adaptado, dirigida a personas con grandes necesidades de apoyo físico y en la que España cuenta con una consolidada trayectoria internacional. La boccia, como la petanca, se juega sobre una pista rectangular en la que los jugadores tratan de lanzar unas bolas lo más cerca posible de una pelota blanca, al tiempo que se intenta alejar las de sus rivales, y posee distintas clases y tipos de lanzamiento en función de la discapacidad de sus participantes. Una audiencia que se celebró a través de la Federación Española de Deporte de Personas con Parálisis Cerebral y Daño Cerebral Adquirido, que compite en el circuito internacional y paralímpico de esta disciplina, cuyos responsables han estado acompañados por técnicos y personal de apoyo que forman parte del combinado nacional. Los deportistas explicaron a la reina el trabajo que llevan a cabo para impulsar esta modalidad, además de destacar el valor del deporte como herramienta de inclusión y visibilidad para las personas con discapacidad y han compartido con ella los recientes éxitos cosechados en la World Boccia Cup de São Paulo, una de las principales citas del calendario internacional. La delegación han destacado además la importancia del acompañamiento técnico y humano en una disciplina en la que auxiliares, entrenadores y personal de apoyo desempeñan un papel fundamental en la preparación y competición de los deportistas. Los jugadores hicieron una demostración práctica de este deporte, a la que se sumó la reina, que también saludó con un abrazo a una de las deportistas, Sara Aller Mayo, a la que conoció durante la celebración de los Juegos Paralímpicos. Antes, la reina recibió también en el Palacio de La Zarzuela a la selección española de balonmano en silla de ruedas, que el pasado 20 de septiembre de 2026 se proclamó campeona del mundo por primera vez en su historia tras imponerse a Japón en la final. Durante el encuentro, compartieron con la reina sus experiencias en el campeonato celebrado en Granollers, así como el trabajo realizado para lograr este título histórico. También hablaron de cómo han vivido estos dos meses que han pasado desde su consecución, la repercusión del Mundial en Granollers en los ámbitos organizativo y deportivo, y de su próximo objetivo: el Campeonato Europeo. La reina recibió una camiseta de la selección con su nombre y un juego conmemorativo de medallas del Campeonato del Mundo.

articles.title: 4 predictions for Bills vs. Chiefs on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills may lean heavily on a ground-and-pound offensive attack to combat weather, Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving
articles.body:
Is there anything bold to predict about a powerhouse matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs? Sure, given enough imagination and luck. Bills-Chiefs on Thanksgiving night is truly must-see TV.

You can bet that most of the country will be tuned in this evening to see what quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes have in store for Round 11. Through 10 games (includes playoffs), Allen and Mahomes are each 5-5. The key difference between them is that Allen has gone 4-1 in the regular season, while Mahomes has gone 4-0 in the postseason.

That said, this is a regular season with huge stakes. Buffalo is currently 9-1 and in first place in the AFC, but this game's winner takes the driver's seat over the loser in the chase for the one seed come playoff time. Well that is, unless they finish in a tie.

As you might expect, there are a lot of similarities between the Bills and Chiefs. Beyond the well-known star players, however, the rosters are a bit different. Where they run parallel is at quarterback — thanks to the two best players of this generation. Buffalo and Kansas City also boast nasty rushing attacks, and the Bills have the league's top-ranked unit behind lead running back James Cook III.

These are two teams that like to bleed clock, but can strike 80 yards or more down the field for six in a moment's notice. Tonight, the recipe might involve a bit more of the running game from both sides, at least until it's safer to attack downfield in the passing game.

Here are four bold predictions I have for the Bills on Thanksgiving…

James Cook sets new career high in rushing attempts

You may have heard by now that the Bills are a run-first offense. That fact hasn't necessarily limited what Allen can accomplish as a passer, but head coach Joe Brady is intent on establishing dominance in the trenches.

Somewhere along the line, Cook must have been told that he'd be a fantastic runner between the tackles, despite his somewhat small size for the position. That, or his instincts know ball. Maybe it's both, and it might also be true that Buffalo's offensive line opens up some tasty running lanes between the tackles.

Whatever the case may be, Cook is a dangerous one-cut, take-it-to-the-house runner who, in ways, recalls Terrel Davis. Last season's rushing yardage champion has taken on an even bigger role in the Bills' offense this season, and he's currently second in rushing yards.

I predict a heavy workload for Cook tonight, with him setting a new personal best in carries. That number to beat is 32, which he set almost one year ago against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cook has already come close to breaking that number, having totaled 31 carries against the Minnesota Vikings this season (Week 9).

It may not seem like a bold prediction, given the expected weather and Cook's role. However, if it comes to be, that may mean that the Bills thoroughly dominated the trenches and stole away the game clock. Buffalo is 14-2 in games that Cook carries the ball 20 or more times, so there's reason to expect they lean on him in bad weather.

FanDuel Sportsbook has James Cook's rushing attempts set at over 18.5 (-138)/under 18.5 (+104). I'd be shocked if he see the ball less than 20 times.

New Bills safety Amani Hooker has fit right in and taken every snap on defense since Buffalo brought him in via trade ahead of Week 10. Hooker has five interceptions on the season, which includes a hat trick against Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow.

The Bills may ask Hooker to spend a lot of time shadowing tight end Travis Kelce, which could mean ample opportunities to steal a ball from Mahomes. Kelce loves to ad-lib routes, and you can bet Hooker has studied his tendencies to see when and where jumping the route may lead to six the other way.

Mahomes has thrown only four interceptions this season, and none in the past four games. He's due. You can't try to cash in on his odds for a pick-six at FanDuel Sportsbook, but Amani Hooker is currently listed at +1200 to record an interception.

Khalil Shakir leads team in catches and receiving yards

Try as they might, One Bills Drive can't seem to shake Shakir's role as Buffalo's most consistently productive receiver. He isn't always the one with the most yards or catches, but Shakir's efficiency is nearly unmatched.

If anything, Brady and Allen should be working to get Shakir more involved on game day. There were encouraging signs in Week 11 against the Miami Dolphins, when Shakir was involved early, even catching a 38-yard pass downfield while leading the team in receiving yards (101).

I often refer to Shakir as The Pinball Wizard thanks to his insane agility in both space and traffic. He's the best of both worlds as a shifty wide receiver with traits that rival the best running backs.

Brady probably understands that it makes sense to attack the middle of Kansas City's defense, and who better to lead that effort than Shakir? Maybe you prefer tight end Dalton Kincaid? Sure, that's fair game, if he plays through a pair of injuries.

Shakir is currently listed at +600 with FanDuel Sportsbook to finish with the most receiving yards among all players from both teams in the game. Again, with nasty weather expected, it seems reasonable to count on Allen looking to his most reliable receiver. Repeat after me: In Shakir We Trust.

Josh Allen & Patrick Mahomes each run for a TD

It's Allen and Mahomes, and both are surgical dual-threats. You already trust that Allen's running for at least one touchdown. You might scoff at Mahomes doing it simply because the Chiefs never use him in short-yardage situations. It doesn't matter. Mahomes is probably going to end up keeping it himself for six from the red zone once this evening.

You can get in on this as a 2 leg Same Game Parlay at FanDuel Sportsbook, which currently lists Allen and Mahomes as +995 to each score an anytime touchdown (which includes rushing or receiving).

As we know, anything can happen when the Bills hit the field. What are you predictions for Bills-Chiefs in Week 12? Think you've got what it takes to make a play with the Buffalo Bills in 2026? Head over to FanDuel Sportsbook now and put your luck to the test !
